name: 鶏そば十番156（ICHIKORO）
address_ja: 確認できた住所は、〒106-0045 東京都港区麻布十番2-1-10（麻布十番本店、現在閉店）と、〒150-0021 東京都渋谷区恵比寿西1-7-5 篠崎ビル1F（恵比寿店、Uber Eats 上では停止扱い）の2件。どちらも現在営業中であることを確認できなかった。
cuisine: Rich chicken-paitan ramen bar — 純鶏そば, 鶏白湯 with aosa seaweed, triple-stock tsukesoba and a shrimp-hot tantanmen, roughly ¥980–¥1,500 a bowl. Listed here only for the record: the premises this describes are not open.
neighborhood: Light record places it 4 min from Ebisu Station (JR Yamanote/Saikyo, Tokyo Metro Hibiya). The Ebisu branch address on Uber Eats is Ebisu-nishi 1-7-5, Shibuya-ku; the brand's verifiable home is Azabu-juban 2-1-10, Minato-ku (Azabu-juban Station, Oedo/Namboku lines). Neither is confirmed trading.
hours_raw: 日〜火 11:00〜23:00（L.O.22:…） — as still published on the Azabu-juban honten's Instagram bio; not verified against an open door.
gf_detail: Wheat is the dish. The noodle is a wheat noodle — the Ebisu branch's own Uber Eats copy says 「北海道産小麦を使用した麺」 (noodles made with Hokkaido wheat) — the tare and the tsukesoba dip are soy-sauce based, and the shop also runs tantanmen and mazesoba out of the same pots. There is no gluten-free item, no wheat-free noodle and no published allergen handling. A celiac has nothing to eat here.
vegan_detail: The entire concept is chicken paitan — a stock boiled from chicken bones — with a 鶏豚魚介 (chicken, pork and fish) triple stock on the tsukesoba. Nothing on the published menu is plant-based.

chef_bio.background: Treat this as a provenance note rather than a bio, because the shop's status is the story. 鶏そば十番156 (read ICHIKORO, a pun on 一コロ — 'you'll be floored in one') opened as a self-styled Ramen & bar on the Azabu-juban shopping street, at Azabu-juban 2-1-10, phone 03-3453-1560; it is still carried in the Azabu-juban Shopping Street Association's member directory at those details, with the association's own coordinates 35.65533 / 139.73621. Tabelog, however, files the Azabu-juban honten as 【閉店】 and carries a reviewer's account of a farewell visit — 「移転準備のため12/21をもって閉店するとのことで、最終日に…訪問しました。移転先も同じ麻布十番エリアとのこと」 (closed 21 December to prepare for a move, said to be relocating within Azabu-juban). I could not find the reopened address. A Chofu branch, 鶏そば十番156 トリエ京王調布店 (Chofu, Kojima-cho 2-61-1), still has a Tabelog page. The Ebisu branch this record would correspond to exists only as an Uber Eats storefront named 「ZZZ 鶏そは十番156恵比寿店」 at Ebisu-nishi 1-7-5, Shinozaki Building 1F — the ZZZ prefix is Uber Eats' marker for a deactivated store — and it does not appear anywhere in Tabelog's Ebisu ramen listing. The brand is also absent from the current brand/store list of Food Revamp, Inc. (fr-h.co.jp/store), whose page today carries only four brands; a search engine's cached copy of that same page still shows a 鶏蕎麦十番156 トリエ京王調布店 entry, which suggests the brand was dropped from the portfolio rather than that it was never there. No owner or chef is named on any source I opened.
chef_bio.specialty: 純鶏そば / 純鶏あおさそば (chicken paitan with aosa seaweed), 純濃つけそば, 海老辛汁なし担々麺.
chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13168206 marks the Azabu-juban honten 閉店 and carries the 12/21 closure-for-relocation review. The Azabu-juban Shopping Street Association directory still lists the shop at 麻布十番2-1-10 / 03-3453-1560. Uber Eats lists the Ebisu branch at 恵比寿西1-7-5 篠崎ビル1F under a ZZZ-prefixed (deactivated) store name and quotes the Hokkaido-wheat noodle copy. Tabelog's Ebisu ramen listing contains no 156 entry. Food Revamp's live brand page no longer carries the brand.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A one-pot ramen kitchen running wheat noodles, mazesoba and tantanmen. Nothing here is protected from wheat and nothing is claimed to be.

cultural_comfort.note: Do not put this on an itinerary. The Azabu-juban honten closed on 21 December to relocate and I could not find the new address; the Ebisu storefront this record points at survives only as a deactivated Uber Eats listing and appears in no restaurant directory. If the record is kept at all, it should be kept as a lead to re-check, not as a place to walk to.

enrich_note: NAME CORRECTION. The light record read 「鶏蕎麦 十番」 at Ebisu. No business of that bare name exists; the shop the name is a garbling of is 鶏そば十番156 (ICHIKORO), a chicken-paitan ramen bar. Two caveats that matter more than the correction: (a) the brand's home is Azabu-juban 2-1-10, Minato-ku, not Ebisu — the Ebisu branch (渋谷区恵比寿西1-7-5 篠崎ビル1F) exists only as a ZZZ-prefixed, i.e. deactivated, Uber Eats storefront and is absent from Tabelog's Ebisu ramen listing; (b) Tabelog marks the Azabu-juban honten 閉店, closed 21 December to prepare a move within Azabu-juban, and I could not find where it reopened. Coordinates left unchanged, loc_precise:false, confidence low. RECOMMEND: hold or delete pending confirmation that any 156 storefront is trading. Also note an alternative I could not rule out — Ebisu does have a chicken-stock soba shop, 親鶏中華そば 綾川 本店 (298 m from Ebisu Station) — which the sweep could equally have been groping at.

chef_bio.background: Could not be established. Two independent searches were negative for a Tokyo 鰻 ひろ川. A Yahoo Japan search for 鰻 ひろ川 恵比寿 東京 returns Ebisu's actual eel shops — うなぎ 登川 (渋谷区恵比寿西1-15-2 アパルトマンイトウ1F, Ebisu Station 3–4 min, a shop the Ebisu Shimbun dates to about 60 years and traces back to a Shimbashi eel house) and 恵比寿 鰻 松川 (渋谷区恵比寿南2-21-7, by Ebisu Garden Place, Ebisu Station 4 min) — but nothing by this name. A nationwide search for 「うなぎ ひろ川」 / 「鰻 廣川」 returns one restaurant only, うなぎ屋 廣川 in Kyoto (京都市右京区嵯峨天龍寺北造路町44-1, Arashiyama), plus a Nakameguro Sanuki-udon shop 讃岐うどん ひろ川 and an Osaka steakhouse 肉匠 ひろ川. A Brave search for 「鰻 ひろ川」恵比寿 returns only 松川 and 新宿うな鐵 恵比寿店. On the evidence, either the sweep invented the name or it garbled 松川 or 登川 — both of which end in 川 and both of which sit the stated 3–4 minutes from Ebisu Station. I am not willing to pick between them, so no name correction has been made.

name: 虎ノ門 大坂屋 砂場
address_ja: 〒105-0001 東京都港区虎ノ門１丁目10-6
cuisine: Edo soba in a 1923 wooden house that is a Registered Tangible Cultural Property — fine, square-cut nihachi from Hokkaido buckwheat, shiba-shrimp kakiage seiro and a long shochu-and-sake list; ¥1,000 for a plain mori, ¥1,500–¥2,400 for the tempura seiro, cash only
neighborhood: Toranomon 1-chome, Minato-ku — 3 min from Toranomon Station exit 1 (Tokyo Metro Ginza line), 5 min from Kasumigaseki (exits C2/C3), 8 min from Shimbashi's Hibiya gate; 226 m from Toranomon Station, in the shadow of Toranomon Hills
hours_raw: 月、火、水 11:00～14:00／16:30～19:30　木、金 11:00～14:00／16:30～20:00　※ただし、昼夜ともお蕎麦売り切れの際は、閉店させていただきます。　定休日：土曜日、日曜日、祝日
gf_detail: Wheat is structural and there is no gluten-free line. The house soba is nihachi — 80% buckwheat to 20% wheat flour, which reviewers describe as 「砂場伝統の二八」 — so even the plain もりそば is not gluten-free, and the board dusting is wheat uchiko. The tsuyu is soy-sauce based, and no tamari or wheat-free soy is mentioned anywhere. The kitchen deep-fries wheat-battered tempura all service (車海老の天種, 芝海老のかき揚げ, ごぼうのかき揚げ), runs a katsudon and a katsu-ni in wheat breadcrumbs, and lists 麦焼酎 — barley shochu, 兼八 and 百年の孤独 — on the drinks card. The site publishes no allergen page and makes no claim. Treat this as a firm no.
vegan_detail: No. The tsuyu is a bonito-and-soy dashi, the soba itself contains wheat, and the vegetable-sounding dishes do not survive inspection: 野菜丼 (¥1,800) and 豆腐カツ丼 (¥900) are donburi built on the same dashi and egg, おろしそば and とろろそば are both marked 卵黄入り (with egg yolk), ごぼうの天せいろは wheat-and-egg batter, and そばみそ (¥450) and 焼き海苔 (¥710) are the only two plates on the card that might be plant-based — and even those are seasoned with the house soy. There is no vegan set and no plant-based tsuyu.

roles: 砂場会 member house — the trade body founded by the fourth generation
chef_bio.origin: Toranomon, Minato-ku — the family has traded on this ground since 1872, on land ceded from the estate of the former daimyo Abe house
chef_bio.background: This is one of the three great Edo soba lineages, and the shop tells its own history plainly on its site. The trade name 砂場 (sunaba, 'sand yard') goes back to Hideyoshi's time: when Osaka Castle was being built, a confectioner called Izumiya opened a soba stall on the site's sand store, and the name stuck. When the Tokugawa unified the country the business came down to Edo as 大坂屋砂場. In 1872 (Meiji 5) the head house, 糀谷七丁目砂場藤吉, granted a noren-wake to 稲垣よそ, the first generation, and her husband 稲垣音次郎, the second — and Toranomon Osakaya Sunaba began. Yoso was close to the samurai families; the shop received part of the old Abe daimyo estate at founding, and was patronised by the three 'shu' of the Bakumatsu — Yamaoka Tesshū, Takahashi Deishū and Katsu Kaishū. A piece of calligraphy said to have been given by Yamaoka Tesshū still hangs in the room. The Inagaki house rules, quoted on the site, run: 一、人に貸すことなかれ。一、人に借りることなかれ。一、唯一心に勤め励美て家門を思ふべし — neither lend nor borrow, and mind the house with a single heart. The fourth-generation 稲垣勝俊 founded and chaired the 砂場会 to protect the lineage and registered 砂場 and its four kana spellings as trademarks; the fifth, 稲垣隆一, chaired it after him; the sixth, 稲垣隆俊, runs the shop today. The building itself was put up in 1923 (Taishō 12), survived the wartime air raids, the Great Kanto and the Tohoku earthquakes, and was registered as a Tangible Cultural Property in 1996 — the shop's English page gives that date. The soba is stone-milled Hokkaido buckwheat cut nihachi, square in section and fine in grain; the sake list runs to eighteen labels including Den-shu, Isojiman Aiyama and Tedorigawa, and the shochu selection leans on buckwheat shochu served cut with sobayu. Eighty seats over two floors, tatami rooms for four to eight, all non-smoking since April 2015, and cash only — no cards, no e-money, no QR payment.
chef_bio.philosophy: Keep the lineage and keep the house: neither lend nor borrow, mind the trade with a single heart, and close when the soba runs out rather than stretch it.
chef_bio.specialty: もりそば ¥1,000; 芝海老のかき揚げ天せいろ ¥2,200; 白えびの天せいろ ¥2,400; 鴨せいろ ¥2,300; 花巻そば (nori and fresh wasabi) ¥1,500; かつ丼（もち豚） ¥1,600; そばみそ ¥450 and 板わさ ¥800 to drink over; buckwheat shochu ¥650–¥780 a glass, cut with sobayu.

anecdotes.text: The name predates the shop by nearly three centuries: a confectioner named Izumiya opened a soba stall on the sand store of the Osaka Castle building site, and the trade has been called 砂場 — 'the sand yard' — ever since.

The first-generation owner Inagaki Yoso received part of the former Abe daimyo estate when she founded the shop and was patronised by Yamaoka Tesshū, Takahashi Deishū and Katsu Kaishū; a scroll attributed to Yamaoka still hangs in the dining room.
The 1923 building came through the wartime air raids and both the Great Kanto and Tohoku earthquakes, and was listed as a Registered Tangible Cultural Property in 1996.
Both lunch and dinner end the moment the day's soba is gone — the shop says so on every page — and at busy lunchtimes you will be asked to share a table.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: toranomon-sunaba.com carries the address 〒105-0001 東京都港区虎ノ門１丁目10-6, the phone 03-3501-9661, the hours and Sat/Sun/holiday closure, the cash-only policy, the full priced menu across six category pages, and the /history page with the 砂場 origin story, the 1872 noren-wake from 糀谷七丁目砂場藤吉, the Inagaki generations one through six by name, the house rules and the 1923 building; the English page adds the 1996 cultural-property registration. Tabelog 13002143 supplies the exact coordinates 35.668232 / 139.750713, the 1872 opening date, 80 seats with private tatami rooms for 4/6/8, all-non-smoking since April 2015, no cards or e-money, a note that the shop moved here from 港区西新橋1-10-1, the Hokkaido-buckwheat and square-cut description, the eighteen sake labels, and a reviewer's confirmation that the soba is 砂場伝統の二八 and the building a registered cultural property.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The noodle itself is 20% wheat flour and the boards are dusted with wheat uchiko; the tempura fryer runs shiba-shrimp, kuruma-prawn, kisu, burdock and yam batter through every service, and a tonkatsu is on the card. There is nothing wheat-free to protect.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Tsuyu, tare and the simmered dishes are all soy-sauce based and no gluten-free tamari is named anywhere on the site.

Barley is on the drinks list too: 兼八 and 百年の孤独 are 麦焼酎, barley shochu. Order the buckwheat shochu (佐久の花, 木火土金水, 蕎麦和尚, 八重桜) if the distinction matters — though the sobayu it is cut with comes off the same wheat-carrying noodles.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bonito dashi under the tsuyu; おろしそば and とろろそば are marked 卵黄入り (egg yolk added); the fryer handles prawn, kisu and eel-adjacent items alongside the vegetable tempura.

positives.text: There is a full English page with an English menu and translated dish descriptions — unusual for a shop of this vintage — and the shop says it looks forward to overseas guests.
All seats non-smoking since 1 April 2015, 80 seats across tables and tatami with private rooms for four, six or eight, and children are welcome.

cultural_comfort.note: An old wooden house three minutes from Toranomon Station with an English page, an English menu and staff used to foreign visitors — the door is not intimidating and the room is the reason to come. Two things to plan around. First, it is cash only: no credit cards, no IC money, no QR payment, and the shop states this twice on its own site. Second, it keeps office hours — closed Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays, dinner ending at 19:30 Monday to Wednesday and 20:00 Thursday and Friday — and both services stop the moment the day's soba sells out, so go early. At busy lunchtimes you will be asked to share a table. Reservations are accepted by phone (03-3501-9661).

enrich_note: NAME CORRECTION — and a neighbourhood correction, which needs a human's eye. The light record read 「大坂屋 そば店」 at Azabu-juban. There is no 大坂屋 in Azabu-juban: the Azabu-juban Shopping Street Association's own member directory (398 shops, checked in full) contains no such name, and Yahoo Japan searches for 麻布十番 大坂屋 そば店 return the district's real soba houses (麻布永坂 更科本店, 永坂更科 布屋太兵衛 麻布総本店, 総本家 更科堀井) and nothing else. Tokyo's only 大坂屋 soba house is 虎ノ門 大坂屋 砂場, 1.9 km away at 港区虎ノ門１丁目10-6 — same ward, founded 1872, a Registered Tangible Cultural Property building, and squarely inside the 3-mile sweep radius. I have enriched under the corrected name and moved the pin to Tabelog's exact coordinates for that address (35.668232 / 139.750713), so loc_precise is now true. The identification rests on name plus genre plus ward, not on a source that links the two records, which is why confidence is medium rather than high: if the merge policy is not to relocate a pin on inference, drop this record instead of shipping it at the old Azabu-juban coordinates. Genre note for the ranking pass: the soba is nihachi and the drinks list carries barley shochu, so gf_confidence is 'no', not 'ask'.
